body:
## Problem

`pip wheel .` reuses setuptools' `server/build/` directory across releases. That
directory is only ever added to — files deleted from `src/` since the last build
survive in it and get packaged again.

Caught while cutting 1.6.0: the wheel shipped BOTH the new `web_dist/assets/
index-DvP9MrsH.js` and the previous release's `index-BHB07Egq.js`, even though
the latter no longer exists in the working tree. Fixed for 1.6.0 by
`rm -rf server/build` before `pip wheel`.

Almost certainly affected 1.5.0 (and likely earlier releases) the same way —
each would carry its predecessor's bundle.

## Impact

Cosmetic/size only, not a correctness bug: `web_dist/index.html` references the
current bundle by hash, so the stale file is never served — it's dead weight
(~280 KB/release, compounding). Worth fixing because a stale `build/` is exactly
the mechanism that WOULD ship a wrong file if a future release renamed or
removed something the running code loads by path rather than by hash.

## Fix

Add `rm -rf server/build server/dist` to the release steps before `pip wheel`
(or switch to `python -m build`, which builds in an isolated temp dir by
default — note `build` isn't currently installed in the server venv).

If a release checklist/script exists, put it there; otherwise this ticket is the
record. Consider also asserting in a test that the wheel's `web_dist/assets/`
contains exactly the files referenced by its `index.html`.
title: Release wheels carry stale files from a reused setuptools build/ dir
